title: Remote tier executor: the task the service queues and the result the agent posts back
description: interfaces.md section 27 (CR-WG-executor; David 2026-10-16 decision 1). The service queues a task (one capability of one tree at one commit); a pull agent on the EDA host claims it over the POST-only executor API, lays the commit out from its read-only mirror, runs `run.command` sandboxed and unprivileged, and posts a result. The documents are the queue's own records; nothing here is a registry file. Owner: executor.queue (server), executor.agent (agent).

argv_or_shell.description: A shell string (run by /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c) or an argv list. Never one that sources a set_env.sh (refused on both sides).

tree_path.description: A path inside the laid-out tree: relative, no `..` part, no leading slash.

task.description: What the service asks one agent to run. `mirror` and every pin's `mirror` are catalogue entry ids: the agent finds `<mirror_root>/<id>.git`, a read-only replica of the service's own mirror (interfaces.md section 3 layout). The commit must already be in it; the agent never fetches from a host.

subject.description: What the run is evidence for. `configuration` may be null for a component-only run (a capability of a tree that is no registered configuration).

side.description: A paired bump run (interfaces section 27.6): which side of the pair this task is.

pair.description: The id both sides of a paired run share.

pins.description: Submodule checkouts laid out inside the root, outermost first. Empty: the root alone.

env.description: Explicit environment for the command, on top of the sandbox's clean one. `${TREE}` and earlier entries expand. May not set TREE, HOME, PATH or any NANOSOC_RM_* variable.

verdict.description: How the result is judged. Exit `exit` (default 0) alone is PASS only when no `forbid` string appears in the output; a declared `verdicts` file (toolkit verdicts.tsv, tree-relative) adds its rows.

control.description: A negative control, run after the command in the same tree: it must exit non-zero (the gate can fail). A control that exits 0 makes the run UNVERIFIED.

labels.description: Every label the claiming agent must carry ([[executor.agents]] labels): the tools the command needs (vcs, xcelium, verilator, genus ...).

claim.description: The answer to POST /executor/v1/claim when a task is handed out.

job_claim.description: The answer to POST /executor/v1/claim when a tier JOB of the local job queue is handed out (interfaces section 27.6; the job kinds are the capabilities unit's, section 26). The agent runs `nanosoc-rm <argv>` with its own nanosoc-rm config, sandboxed, and posts {lease, exit_code, stdout, log} to /executor/v1/jobs/<job_id>/result.

result.description: What the agent posts to /executor/v1/tasks/<id>/result. Every row carries the task's nonce. A result whose nonce or lease does not match the current claim is refused (409).

sandbox.description: bwrap: bubblewrap namespaces (no home, no ssh, read-only tools). fallback: scrubbed environment only (interfaces section 27.4, residual risk).
